A program prepares a draft route: places the author writes about as visited, with supporting paragraphs. Then each book is read: only the places where the author actually was remain, in the order of the journey, with a verbatim quotation; quotations and paragraph numbers are checked against the text automatically. The project's experts confirm routes in the team workspace; the map shows which routes have already been confirmed

The resource combines expert philological work with the sources and digital processing of the corpus. The selection of books, their description, the dictionary of names of peoples, the reconstruction of routes, the annotation of evaluations and relations and the interpretation of results were done by researchers; programs were used where all # million words had to be gone through, and each of their results was checked by hand

The resource grew out of a study of how inter-ethnic relations in Siberia were perceived in European travelogues of the 19th and early 20th centuries. The corpus was compiled from bibliographic reference works and the holdings of digital libraries, annotated by experts and processed with the methods of corpus linguistics; for details, see
Siberian State University of Geosystems and Technologies

Left: the network of groups; an edge connects groups named in one sentence of a paragraph about Siberia (thickness: the number of such sentences). Right, via the switch: the intertextual network — who cites whom and who borrows from whom. The graph is three-dimensional: you can rotate it, zoom in and drag nodes; clicking a node opens its card
